main_text.p: His tamen obstat, quod ad Principem non pateat nisi per Ministros ejus aditus: major his quàm Principi arrogantia & impotentius fastidium: qui tunc demum egregiè se tutariDomini sui dignitatem arbitrantur, si quod ingenuum erat & non fictum, id omne tamquam læsæ majestatis suspectum represserint, si quod sine majorum imaginibus probum ac industrium, id omne tamquam plebeium & profanum à Principis sacrario repulerint: Hos sibi devinciat qui Deo vel notus esse voluerit: scis quo pacto? Assentationibus, servilibus blanditiis, donis, promissis, sordibus. Quod si hæc condicio minus æqua videatur & Philosophiæ legibus adversari, ævum teras necquicquam, atria quotidianis discursibus fatiges, & inter leviculam illam Aulæ juventutem explo-

page.notes: The line "explo-" is the catchword-like hyphenated continuation, set right-aligned; it is part of the text. Show-through and edge fragments of the facing page are present at the left and were omitted. Some letters are uncertain due to scan quality in "tutariDomini" (printed as one word in the original) and "sine majorum" (printed as "finemajorum").
